To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the angular distribution of radiation emitted from a cloud of particles can be predicted by the use of the Mie theory and that the angular distribution is strongly influenced by the scattering properties of the cloud particles.

the angular distribution of thermal radiation from a cloud of particles is strongly influenced by the scattering properties of the individual particles and by the size of the particle cloud relative to the wavelength of the radiation.

the angular distribution of radiation emitted by a particle cloud depends on the ratio of the cloud's radius to its mean particle diameter, the optical thickness of the cloud, and the scattering properties of the particles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the angular distribution of thermal radiation from a cylindrical particle cloud in a vacuum.

the angular distribution of the radiation emitted by an isothermal cloud of spherical particles, and with the effects of the particle size, the scattering properties, and the optical thickness of the cloud on the angular distribution of this radiation.
the angular distribution of the radiation emitted from the surface of a cylindrical particle cloud, which is heated to incandescence by a laser beam of given power.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the case of a cylindrical particle cloud, the anisotropy of the angular radiation distribution is not significant in determining the total radiant energy emitted by the cloud, but is significant in determining the direction from which that energy is received.
the radiation from a cylindrical particle cloud, with the exception of the forward direction, can be considered as being isotropically scattered.
the anisotropic scattering of radiation from a cylindrical particle cloud is a function of the cloud radius, particle radius, and scattering coefficient of the particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radiation intensity from a cylindrical particle cloud is strongly dependent on the scattering characteristics.
the angular distribution of the radiation from a cylindrical particle cloud is not significantly altered by scattering, but that the intensity of the radiation is greatly increased.
the angular distribution of the radiation from a cylindrical cloud of particles depends on the particle size and shape, the scattering phase function, and the optical depth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the angular distribution of the thermal radiation from a cylindrical cloud is very different from the angular distribution from an equivalent sphere.
the angular distribution of thermal radiation from a particle cloud can be significantly affected by scattering.
, for anisotropic scattering, the angular distribution of the thermal radiation from a particle cloud depends on the ratio of the particle diameter to the cloud diameter.
